arxiv-2101-08464.title: Programming Boundary Deformation Patterns in Active Networks
arxiv-2101-08464.creator: Zijie Qu 1 , Jialong Jiang 1 , Heun Jin Lee 2 , Rob Phillips 1,2,3, Shahriar Shadkhoo 1, Matt Thomson 1
arxiv-2101-08464.description: Abstract Active materials take advantage of their internal sources of energy to self-organize in an automated manner. This feature provides a novel opportunity to design micron-scale machines with minimal required control. However, self-organization goes hand in hand with predetermined dynamics that are hardly susceptible to environmental perturbations.

arxiv-2103-00398.title: Canonical subsheaves of torsionfree semistable sheaves
arxiv-2103-00398.creator: Indranil Biswas, A. J. Parameswaran
arxiv-2103-00398.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Indranil Biswas, A. J. Parameswaran. Let F F be a torsionfree semistable coherent sheaf on a polarized normal projective variety defined over an algebraically closed field. We prove that F F has a unique maximal locally free subsheaf V V such that F / V F/V is torsionfree and V V also admits a filtration of subbundles for which each successive quotient is a stable vector bundle whose slope is μ ⁡ ( F ) \mu(F) .

arxiv-2103-09656.title: Set-to-Sequence Methods in Machine Learning: a Review
arxiv-2103-09656.creator: Mateusz Jurewicz maju@itu.dk, mj@tjek.com, Leon Derczynskileod@itu.dk
arxiv-2103-09656.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mateusz Jurewicz maju@itu.dk, mj@tjek.com, Leon Derczynskileod@itu.dk. Machine learning on sets towards sequential output is an important and ubiquitous task, with applications ranging from language modelling and meta-learning to multi-agent strategy games and power grid optimization. Combining elements of representation learning and structured prediction, its two primary challenges include obtaining a meaningful, permutation invariant set representation and subsequently utilizing this representation to output a complex target permutation.

arxiv-2103-12807.title: Magnetic field-assisted spectral decomposition and imaging of charge states of NV centers in diamond
arxiv-2103-12807.creator: T. Chakraborty 1,2 , R. Bhattacharya 3 , V. S. Anjusha 3,4 , M. Nesladek 5,6 , D. Suter 1,3 and T. S. Mahesh 3
arxiv-2103-12807.description: Abstract With the advent of quantum technology, nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers in diamond turn out to be a frontier which provides an efficient platform for quantum computation, communication and sensing applications. Due to the coupled spin-charge dynamics of the NV system, knowledge about NV charge state dynamics can help to formulate efficient spin control sequences strategically.

arxiv-2207-10796.title: Multiple Robust Learning for Recommendation
arxiv-2207-10796.creator: Haoxuan Li, Quanyu Dai, Yuru Li, Yan Lyu, Zhenhua Dong, Xiao-Hua Zhou, Peng Wu
arxiv-2207-10796.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Haoxuan Li, Quanyu Dai, Yuru Li, Yan Lyu, Zhenhua Dong, Xiao-Hua Zhou, Peng Wu. In recommender systems, a common problem is the presence of various biases in the collected data, which deteriorates the generalization ability of the recommendation models and leads to inaccurate predictions. Doubly robust (DR) learning has been studied in many tasks in RS, with the advantage that unbiased learning can be achieved when either a single imputation or a single propensity model is accurate.

arxiv-2507-11778.title: Without microphysical causation, just anything cannot begin to exist just anywhere
arxiv-2507-11778.creator: Daniel Linford
arxiv-2507-11778.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Daniel Linford. According to the Causal Principle, anything that begins to exist has a cause. In turn, various authors – including Thomas Hobbes, Jonathan Edwards, and Arthur Prior – have defended the thesis that, had the Causal Principle been false, there would be no good explanation for why entities do not begin at arbitrary times, in arbitrary spatial locations, in arbitrary number, or of arbitrary kind. I call this the Hobbes-Edwards-Prior Principle (HEPP).

arxiv-2508-12664.title: Real-Analyticity of the Density of States for Random Schrödinger operators with Point Interactions
arxiv-2508-12664.creator: Masahiro Kaminaga
arxiv-2508-12664.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Masahiro Kaminaga. We prove real-analyticity of the density of states (DOS) for random Schrödinger operators with lattice-supported point interactions in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} ( d = 1 , 2 , 3 d=1,2,3 ) in the small-hopping regime. In the attractive case, Krein’s resolvent formula reduces the problem to a lattice model, where a random-walk expansion and disorder averaging lead to single-site integrals with holomorphic single-site density g g .

pmc-10518448.creator: Gianluca Ferini, Stefano Pergolizzi
pmc-10518448.description: authors pooled the data from 17 studies, 10 of which have also a parallel arm treated with standard fractionation of 2 Gy/day. pmc-10674410.title: Exploring the Association between Delirium and Malnutrition in COVID-19 Survivors: A Geriatric Perspective
pmc-10674410.creator: Sarah Damanti, Marta Cilla, Giordano Vitali, Valeria Tiraferri, Chiara Pomaranzi, Giulia De Rubertis, Rebecca De Lorenzo, Giuseppe Di Lucca, Raffaella Scotti, Emanuela Messina, Raffaele Dell’Acqua, Monica Guffanti, Paola Cinque, Antonella Castagna, Patrizia Rovere-Querini, Moreno Tresoldi
pmc-10674410.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Older individuals face an elevated risk of developing geriatric syndromes when confronted with acute stressors like COVID-19. We assessed the connection between in-hospital delirium, malnutrition, and frailty in a cohort of COVID-19 survivors. Patients aged ≥65, hospitalized in a tertiary hospital in Milan for SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia, were enrolled and screened for in-hospital delirium with the 4 ‘A’s Test (4AT) performed twice daily (morning and evening) during hospital stay.

pmc-12722236.title: Metabolomics and sensomics reveal non-volatile flavor dynamics in summer–autumn steamed green tea flakes processing
pmc-12722236.creator: Zixin Ni, Hongjing Pan, Yiqin Chen, Jiayi Chen, Wangjing Wu, Wei Chen, Yuefei Wang, Jihong Zhou
pmc-12722236.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Summer-autumn steamed green tea flakes have attracted attention as a cost-effective extended product of traditional spring shaded Tencha, but their metabolic and sensory transformations during processing remain unexplored. This study employed non-targeted metabolomics and sensomics approaches, including quantitative descriptive analysis, electronic tongue evaluation, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis—to systematically investigate the dynamic non-volatile metabolic transformations and their associations with sensory attributes. A total of 228 metabolites were significantly correlated with sensory traits.
